record.context_brief: In-dominating sets with small chromatic number
record.original_question: Does every digraph D of maximum out-degree k contain an in-dominating set X such that the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph induced by X is at most log k? Here, an in-dominating set means a set X such that every vertex outside X has at least one out-neighbor in X.

evidence.quote: An in-dominating set X of a digraph D is a subset of vertices of D such that every vertex not in X has at least one out-neigbour in X.
Does every digraph D with maximal out-degree k admit an in-dominating set X with χ(D[X]) ≤ log k (where χ is the usual chromatic number of the underlying graph) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite digraph. For a vertex $v\in V$, the out-neighborhood of $v$ is $N^+(v)=\{u\in V:(v,u)\in E\}$, and the out-degree of $v$ is $|N^+(v)|$. The maximum out-degree of $D$ is $\Delta^+(D)=\max_{v\in V}|N^+(v)|$. A subset $X\subseteq V$ is called an in-dominating set of $D$ if every vertex $v\in V\setminus X$ has at least one out-neighbor in $X$ (i.e. $N^+(v)\cap X\neq\emptyset$). For $X\subseteq V$, let $D[X]$ denote the sub-digraph induced by $X$, and let $\chi(D[X])$ denote the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph of $D[X]$ (obtained by ignoring edge directions and removing multiplicities).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $k\ge 2$ and every digraph $D$ with maximum out-degree at most $k$, there exists an in-dominating set $X\subseteq V(D)$ such that
$$\chi(D[X])\le \log_2 k.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source that resolves or directly addresses this specific question about the existence of an in-dominating set $X$ in a digraph of maximum out-degree $k$ with $\chi(D[X])\le\log k$. While there is active research on dichromatic numbers, domination in digraphs, and related extremal questions, no published proof or counterexample for this particular bound was located, so the current status appears unverified.
